操.meaning: A crane driver hooks an <part>anchor</part> under a kids' <part>treehouse</part> and swings it over three gardens, past washing lines and a startled cat, then lowers it gently into the new oak. The neighbours clap. That's a tricky <kanji>maneuver</kanji>.
操.on: The kids inside blow <sound>soa</sound>p bubbles the whole way over.
操.kun: A <sound>mee</sound>rkat in a <sound>sa</sound>ri guards the new treehouse with her pet <sound>o</sound>tter and never leaves its side: loyalty.

績.meaning: A palace seamstress always got the <part>blame</part> for every rip in the royal robes. So she stitches a tapestry of her best repairs in gold <part>thread</part>: patched capes, mended crowns, a dragon sewn back together. The king hangs it in the hall. It shows all her <kanji>exploits</kanji>.
績.on: Each <sound>sec</sound>tor of the tapestry shows a different year of her work.

剤.meaning: A pharmacist climbs a tall <part>ladder</part> to reach a giant's pill, big as a boulder, and saws off one slice with a <part>dagger</part>. 'Too much,' she mutters, and shaves off a crumb. A mouse with a cold swallows it. Just the right <kanji>dose</kanji>.
剤.on: Cured, the mouse plays a happy tune on a tiny <sound>xy</sound>lophone.
剤.kun: With a <sound>ca</sound>lm hand she snips a loose feather off a <sound>roo</sound>k waiting in line: to trim.

恩.meaning: A grumpy giant who scares everyone quietly fixes the village bridge every night, and won't say what the <part>cause</part> is. One morning the children catch him at it and bake him a pie shaped like a <part>heart</part>. He blushes bright red. Kindness kept secret like his is true <kanji>grace</kanji>.
恩.on: He's so flustered he flicks every <sound>on</sound> switch in the bakery.

刈.meaning: At harvest, the scarecrow is fed up with standing still. He grabs <part>scissors</part> in one hand and a <part>dagger</part> in the other and races through the wheat, snip-snip-slash, stacking sheaves behind him. The farmer wakes to a bare field. The scarecrow loves to <kanji>reap</kanji>.
刈.on: A <sound>gui</sound>de dog leads him back to his post before the crows notice.
刈.kun: Then he stands <sound>ca</sound>lm in the stubble, as if nothing happened.

稲.meaning: In <part>old times</part>, a heron got bored of fish and pushed one <part>claw</part> into the mud, planting a single <part>grain</part>. It sprouted, so she planted more. Now the whole wet valley waves green and her great-grandchildren wade through it. It all began with one <kanji>rice plant</kanji>.
稲.on: She still checks each new sprout by poking it with her <sound>toe</sound>.
稲.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l slips between the stalks, dodging a farmer's <sound>ne</sound>t.

彫.meaning: A sculptor works with a cat curled on his <part>lap</part>, and to pass the time he chisels its portrait into a pumpkin. He gets the ears right, then spends an hour on the <part>whiskers</part>, one fine groove each. The cat yawns and leaves. He's still there, learning to <kanji>carve</kanji>.
彫.on: He finishes the pumpkin cat with a tiny <sound>cho</sound>ker etched round its neck.
彫.kun: Next he chisels a <sound>ho</sound>tdog out of a carrot for lunch.

隠.meaning: At the village fair, a shy dragon has a crush on the baker. She holds up a <part>pennant</part> to hide her face, tucks one <part>claw</part> behind a garden <part>rake</part>, and presses her glowing <part>heart</part> flat against the hay. The baker walks right past. She has a lot to <kanji>conceal</kanji>.
隠.on: She writes him a love note in invisible <sound>in</sound>k.
隠.kun: She slips the note into his <sound>ca</sound>rt, then hides behind the <sound>coo</sound>k.
